```yaml
packages:
  - 'packages/*'
```
```

  tsup.config.ts        # ESM, node18, shebang banner
```

I'll explore your local project and the remote repo in parallel to compare them. Here's what your CLI does that the web-based `tutors-course-builder` does **not**:

## Unique to your project

| Feature | Yours | Theirs |

| **CLI / `npx` scaffolding** | `npx create-tutors-course` — terminal wizard, no browser needed | Web-only (Next.js app), no CLI at all |
| **Headless / SSH / CI usage** | Works in non-GUI environments | Requires a browser |
| **Color-coded placeholders per type** | 5 distinct colors (blue=course, green=topic, peach=talk, plum=lab, yellow=note) | Uniform teal "T" placeholder for everything |
| **Placeholder PDF generation** | Generates minimal valid PDF for talk slides | No PDF placeholders — talks export without a file if none uploaded |
| **Pure-JS image generation** | `pngjs` — zero native deps, no canvas | Uses browser `<canvas>` — only works client-side |
| **Async generator progress** | Yields events per file for real-time progress | ZIP export is all-or-nothing (no progress) |

For context on the PR scope — their web app has: visual tree editor, drag reorder, 15 Lo types (yours has 3: talk/lab/note), ZIP import of existing courses, in-app reader preview, markdown editor with live preview, binary asset management (IndexedDB), course properties editor (companions, iconset, autoNumbering), dark/light theme, and round-trip import/export.

The strongest angle is **adding a CLI companion** to their project — a `create-tutors-course` package that lives alongside the web builder. The value proposition:

1. **Quick bootstrapping** — devs can scaffold a course skeleton in seconds from terminal without opening the web UI
2. **CI/automation** — scriptable course creation
3. **Color-coded placeholders** — visually distinguishable per content type (an improvement over their uniform teal)
4. **PDF placeholders** — talks get a valid placeholder PDF so the exported course is more complete out of the box
